# Copilot Instructions

## Code Quality
- Write clean, concise code — no unnecessary complexity or boilerplate
- Follow the DRY principle; extract repeated logic into reusable functions/classes
- Code must be human-readable; prefer clarity over cleverness
- Keep modules focused and loosely coupled for easy maintenance

## Organization & Naming
- Place new files in appropriate folders that reflect their purpose
- Use intuitive, descriptive names for files, folders, variables, functions, and classes

## Comments
- Comments should be short, precise, and placed only where the intent isn't obvious
- Avoid over-commenting; self-explanatory code needs no comment

## Approach
- Before implementing, think through the approach critically — identify flaws and improve before writing code
- Prefer simple, well-structured solutions over clever or over-engineered ones

## Reports & Documentation
- Avoid generating markdown reports unless necessary
- If a markdown report is needed, limit to one report total

## Memory & Adaptation
- Update these instructions over time based on observed usage patterns and preferences from interactions
